tell: A cholinesterase inhibitor with a half-life near 70 hours that accumulates 4- to 7-fold on once-daily dosing.

clues.text: Absorption is not influenced by food, and about 96% of the drug is bound to plasma protein. It is excreted in urine unchanged and extensively metabolized through CYP2D6 and CYP3A4.
A hydrochloride salt of molecular weight 415.96, soluble in water and in glacial acetic acid.
Approved under an NDA as 5, 10 and 23 mg tablets, taken once daily.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to the drug or to piperidine derivatives; nausea and diarrhea are the most common reasons for stopping.
Dementia of the Alzheimer type, across mild, moderate and severe disease.
A reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase that raises acetylcholine levels, enhancing cholinergic function. There is no evidence it alters the course of the underlying dementia.
The generic name begins with D and has nine letters.
